title: Coforge Ltd - 532541 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Coforge raised FY27 consolidated EBIT margin guidance to 16% from 15.5%, with Q2 EBIT at 16% and a record eight large deals.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was US$652.2 million, up 10.9% sequentially in constant currency, with organic sequential growth of 3.8% CC. Order intake exceeded US$1 billion (up 51% QoQ and 102% YoY), including eight large deals, a quarterly record. Consolidated EBIT margin was 16% and standalone 17%, and management raised FY27 EBIT guidance to 16% and now targets 17% exit in Q4 with more than 17% thereafter. Encora revenue was roughly flat sequentially at about US$147-148 million, and management says Encora growth will mirror Coforge from Q3.

financial_highlights.change: +10.1% QoQ in USD, +10.9% QoQ in CC

financial_highlights.value: US$53.8 million, FCF to PAT 89% in Q2

segments.name: Geography (organic CC QoQ)
segments.commentary: Americas grew 4.1% and rest of world 16.3% sequentially. Order intake was US$455M North America, US$485M Europe, US$101M rest of world.

segments.name: Verticals (organic CC QoQ)
segments.commentary: BFS +8.3%, Insurance +3.6%, Travel/transport/hospitality +1.8%, Emerging verticals +2.3%, Government outside India +20.8%, Healthcare/high-tech -6.4%.

segments.name: Encora
segments.commentary: First full quarter post acquisition; revenue about US$147-148M, roughly flat QoQ. Margin expansion ahead of plan; management expects revenue growth to match Coforge from Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBIT margin raised to 16% from 15.5%; Q4 FY27 reported EBIT targeted at 17%, with more than 17% expected thereafter.
Management said FY28 EBIT margin should be at least the Q4 FY27 exit rate (about 17%).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 20.5%-21% reiterated; FCF to PAT guidance of 100% for FY27 reiterated.
Hedge losses: US$10.2M in Q2; mark-to-market loss guided at US$7.1M in Q3 and US$1.2M in Q4, then zero.
Exceptional items expected at zero from Q3; EPS indicated at about Rs.19-20 in Q4 FY27 (per CFO).
Encora revenue growth to mirror Coforge growth from Q3 FY27; EPS accretion in FY27 reiterated.
capex_capacity: Utilization at 82.4% versus peers at 86%+, cited as a margin lever.
Momentuum Blue forward-deployed engineering unit being built on-site; management expects a material spike in consolidated gross margin from Q3 or starting Q4 due to heavy investment.
AI-led efficiencies in fixed-price contracts expected to show in Q4 margins.
Exceptional costs of US$5.9M in Q2 were for legal entity rationalization (95 entities) and tax structuring; the total acquisition-related spend was about US$17M versus US$15-16M guided.
demand_pricing: Q2 had eight large deals, a company record; management hopes for eight or more in Q3. Deal mix: BFSI 2, public sector 3, high-tech 2, retail 1; by region 3 North America, 4 Europe, 1 rest of world.
Most large deals are sole-sourced, proactive solutions; management says it avoids pricing contests with competitors.
A US$230M UK public sector engagement was signed in July 2026.
Top 5 clients 18.1% of Q2 revenue, top 10 26.4%; top 10 and top 20 accounts growing 20%+ YoY. A second client crossed US$100M annualized run rate.
AI-led engineering, data integration and cloud contributed 86% of revenue.
Largest pipeline deal is with an Encora client; win hoped for in Q3 or Q4.
Management said some AI productivity gains are passed to clients in some deals, but net impact is positive.
Advisory channels are now generating deals that were not previously available.

qa_highlights.question: Are new AI-heavy deals better in tenure and pricing, and do they help margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the second US$100M+ client, which signed a large deal in Q2, is among its highest gross margin clients. Deals are mostly proactive and sole-sourced, avoiding price fights. Current margin uptick is coming from existing fixed-price projects where AI is being infused.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth be sustained at current scale without vendor-driven deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to accelerate growth. It attributes the demand slowdown to fewer procurement-led RFPs. John Speight added that advisory channels are now bringing in deals.

qa_highlights.question: Encora revenue reconciliation and whether it mirrors Coforge growth from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said constant-currency revenue implies about US$657-658M in total, so Encora was about US$147-148M, largely flat from about US$148M (full-quarter equivalent) in Q1. Management confirmed Encora growth will match Coforge's from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is SG&A reduction a trade-off against growth investment, and will gross margin rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no cut to S&M; G&A was up 15.6% YoY against revenue growth of 53%. Growth remains the top priority. Gross margin is expected to spike from Q3 or Q4 as Momentuum Blue investment is absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF to EBITDA fall, and what drives the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to novation of contracts from the US entity to the Indian parent after the Encora deal, which delayed invoicing and collections and raised unbilled revenue. He expects correction and FCF to PAT above 100% by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Minority interest and below-EBIT items?
qa_highlights.answer: Minority interest stays where it is, tied to the Coforge BPS JV in which the client holds 20%. Exceptional items go to zero from Q3; hedge losses fall to US$7.5M in Q3 and US$1.2M in Q4 on mark-to-market.

risks_watch: Gross margin uptick from AI productivity is described as not yet fully on anticipated lines; management expects benefits from Q4.
Pass-through of AI efficiencies to clients in some deals could dilute margins.
Encora revenue was flat QoQ in Q2; delivery of revenue parity from Q3 is a key test.
Organic CC growth was only 3.8% QoQ in Q2 despite strong order intake; the order-to-revenue ramp needs to show in Q3 and Q4.
OCF-to-EBITDA conversion fell due to delayed collections from contract novation; FCF to PAT of 100% for FY27 depends on this recovering.
Healthcare and high-tech declined 6.4% QoQ organically.
Acquisition-related spend ran about US$17M versus US$15-16M guided.
Management expects another record deal quarter in Q3 (eight or more large deals); a shortfall would be a risk.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and assertive on margins, deal momentum and Encora integration, with specific numeric guidance and forward commitments. Answers on AI pass-through economics and gross margin trajectory were more qualitative and less quantified.
key_quotes: We are pleased to raise our consolidated EBIT margin guidance for fiscal year 2027 to 16%, from the 15.5% we had shared at the beginning of the year.
Most of our large deals are sole-sourced and driven by proactive solutions.
There is zero change of heart, there is zero likelihood of there ever being a change of heart.
If we exit at 17%, the least we should deliver next year should be 17%.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 consolidated EBIT margin guidance to 16% from 15.5% and targets 17% in Q4 FY27, backed by a Rs-denominated margin plan (AI-led efficiencies, utilization at 82.4%) and an executable order book of US$2.4bn (+45% YoY) after US$1bn+ order intake, but no new capacity was announced and revenue growth itself was not guided numerically.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management raised FY27 consolidated EBIT guidance to 16% from 15.5%, targets 17% in Q4 FY27 and more than 17% after, with utilisation at 82.4% vs peers 86%+ and AI-led efficiencies in fixed-price contracts expected in Q4 margins; FY28 EBIT at least the ~17% exit rate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order intake above US$1bn (+102% YoY) and a US$2.4bn next-12-month executable order book (+45% YoY) support growth, though Q2 organic sequential growth was only 3.8% CC and Encora revenue is to mirror Coforge growth from Q3.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 82.4%, which is high, but the call gave no capex plan; the Momentuum Blue on-site build is an opex-heavy investment that the company is absorbing into gross margin rather than a capacity announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: EBIT guidance was just raised to 16% from 15.5% with a 17% Q4 exit target, and the executable order book is US$2.4bn, but revenue growth was not guided numerically.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin AI uplift is not yet on anticipated lines, Q2 organic growth was 3.8% CC, OCF-to-EBITDA fell on delayed collections, and Q3 needs eight or more large deals to hold the trajectory.

rows.label: Q3 large-deal run-rate and Encora revenue parity
rows.why: Management hopes for eight or more large deals in Q3 after a record eight in Q2, and expects Encora growth to match Coforge from Q3 after roughly flat revenue of about US$147-148M in Q2.

rows.label: Zero exceptional items from Q3 and hedge losses falling
rows.why: Exceptional items were US$5.9M in Q2 and are guided to zero from Q3, while mark-to-market hedge losses step down to US$7.1M in Q3 and US$1.2M in Q4, then zero.

rows.label: OCF-to-EBITDA recovery and FCF to PAT of 100%
rows.why: Q2 FCF to PAT was 89% and H1 was 92% against FY27 guidance of 100%, with CFO expecting the contract-novation collection delay to correct and FCF to PAT above 100% by year end.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin guidance (16% FY27, 17% Q4), deal momentum and Encora integration, but more qualitative on AI pass-through economics and gross margin timing; analysts pushed on AI-led gross margin uplift and the cash conversion slip.
